 Director at Democratic-leaning firm says early data shows bright spots for both parties 
 Arizona’s ballot count is climbing fast and the numbers reveal why neither party can declare victory yet. By AZFamily Digital News Staff and Dennis Welch Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 5:20 PM MST | Updated : 6 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — About 1.5 million ballots have been cast in Arizona as of Friday morning, roughly half of the total expected turnout this year.
 To review the early numbers, Political Editor Dennis Welch spoke with Adam Kinsey, director at Uplift Campaigns, a Democratic-leaning firm tracking the returns. Kinsey said the data shows bright spots for both parties.
 What the data show for each party
 Democrats are mobilizing first-time voters and banking their reliable base early, Kinsey said.
 Republicans also have reason for optimism, Kinsey said. A large swath of consistent Republican voters has yet to turn in their ballots.
 “What that tells me is there are a lot of Republicans that still have ballots that are expected to vote,” Kinsey said. “So one of two things are happening. One, a bunch of Republicans who ordinarily vote are staying home. Or two, a lot of Republicans are going to be bringing those ballots to the polls on Election Day.”
 What it could mean for Tuesday
 The data signals the potential for a surge of Republican turnout at polling sites on Tuesday.
 If that happens, Democrats would be expected to jump out to an early lead on election night, and Republicans would be expected to close the gap as day-of ballots are counted.
 Welch’s full conversation with Kinsey will air Sunday morning on “Politics Unplugged.”
